Did you know? Porto is famous for its Port wine, which is aged in the cellars of Vila Nova de Gaia, just across the river from the city. Did you know? The Dom Luís I Bridge, an iconic symbol of Porto, was designed by a student of Gustave Eiffel, the creator of the Eiffel Tower. Did you know? Livraria Lello, one of the oldest bookstores in Portugal, is said to have inspired J.K. Rowling while she was writing Harry Potter. Did you know? Porto's São Bento Railway Station is known for its stunning azulejo tile panels that depict historical scenes. Did you know? The Clérigos Tower is one of Porto's most famous landmarks, and climbing its 225 steps rewards you with a panoramic view of the city. Did you know? Porto is home to the oldest wine-producing region in the world, the Douro Valley. Did you know? The Francesinha, a popular Portuguese sandwich covered in melted cheese and a rich tomato sauce, originated in Porto. Did you know? Porto was named "Best European Destination" by the European Consumers Choice in 2012, 2014, and 2017. Did you know? The Church of São Francisco in Porto is famous for its lavish Baroque interior, decorated with over 400 kilograms of gold. Did you know?
